action.description:
The Action to perform when the client connection triggers the rule. Valid actions are:
"allow": allow access to target.
"deny": deny access to target.
"goto_next": forward the request to the next hierarchical policy for evaluation.
"redirect": redirect to a different target. Parameters for this action can be configured via redirectOptions. Only EXTERNAL_302 redirect type is supported for organization security policies.
action.rationale: The action a rule takes (allow/deny/redirect) is a functional/operational choice required for different traffic routing needs (e.g. allow-listing vs deny-listing architectures), not an inherently secure-vs-insecure switch. Enforcing one value globally would break legitimate network designs. Unlike deletion_policy or preview, there is no universal
value here — the security posture comes from how the rule is used within the broader policy set, not from the action value itself.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: If deletion_policy is left at the default value of DELETE, this security rule can be destroyed accidentally via terraform destroy or apply, removing an active access-control enforcement without warning.

description.rationale: description is a free-text label field with no functional effect on rule behaviour, so it carries no security impact.

policy_id.description: The ID of the OrganizationSecurityPolicy this rule applies to.
policy_id.rationale: policy_id is an identifier/reference to the parent OrganizationSecurityPolicy, not a control itself, security is enforced by the rule's own settings, not this pointer.

preview.description: If set to true, the specified action is not enforced.
preview.rationale: Preview is a temporary operational/staging toggle used during rule authoring to test impact before live enforcement, not a fixed security posture. Unlike deletion_policy, a platform-level policy on this field is structurally unworkable: enforcing it to always false would block the mandatory staging step for every rule, while allowing true makes the policy unenforceable. The functional risk of an enforcement rule being left in preview is a deployment-process concern (should be checked before go-live), not something a generic security policy can meaningfully constrain.

priority.description:
An integer indicating the priority of a rule in the list. The priority must be a value
between 0 and 2147483647. Rules are evaluated from highest to lowest priority where 0 is the
highest priority and 2147483647 is the lowest prority.
priority.rationale: Rule priority ordering is an architectural and functional design choice for the team's rule evaluation sequence, not a platform-level security policy target.

header_action.description: Optional, additional actions that are performed on headers.

header_action.request_headers_to_adds.description: The list of request headers to add or overwrite if they're already present.

header_action.request_headers_to_adds.he.description: The name of the header to set.
header_action.request_headers_to_adds.he.rationale: header_name specifies which header to set as part of a functional header-injection action, it does not itself control access, exposure, or data protection.

header_action.request_headers_to_adds.he.description: The value to set the named header to.
header_action.request_headers_to_adds.he.rationale: header_value specifies the value to set for an added header, a functional configuration choice rather than a direct security control.

match.description: A match condition that incoming traffic is evaluated against. If it evaluates to true, the corresponding 'action' is enforced.

match.description.rationale: match.description is a free-text label field with no functional effect on rule behaviour, so it carries no security impact.

match.versioned_expr.description:
Preconfigured versioned expression. For organization security policy rules,
the only supported type is "SRC_IPS_V1".
**NOTE** : 'FIREWALL' type is deprecated. Please use 'google_compute_firewall_policy_rule' resource instead.
match.versioned_expr.rationale: match.versioned_expr is a functional selector enum currently limited to one supported value (SRC_IPS_V1) with no insecure alternative, so no security impact is assigned.

match.config.description: The configuration options for matching the rule.

match.config.src_ip_ranges.description:
Source IP address range in CIDR format. Required for
INGRESS rules.
match.config.src_ip_ranges.rationale: src_ip_ranges directly defines which source IP addresses the rule matches against. An overly broad range (e.g. 0.0.0.0/0 where not intended) directly widens which traffic the rule's action applies to, a direct access-control concern.

match.expr.description: User defined CEVAL expression. A CEVAL expression is used to specify match criteria such as origin.ip, source.region_code and contents in the request header.

match.expr.expression.description: Textual representation of an expression in Common Expression Language syntax. The application context of the containing message determines which well-known feature set of CEL is supported.
match.expr.expression.rationale: The CEL expression defines the actual match logic determining which traffic triggers the rule's action. A misconfigured or overly permissive expression directly changes which requests are allowed, denied, or redirected.

preconfigured_waf_config.description:
Preconfigured WAF configuration to be applied for the rule.
If the rule does not evaluate preconfigured WAF rules, i.e., if evaluatePreconfiguredWaf() is not used, this field will have no effect.

preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.description: An exclusion to apply during preconfigured WAF evaluation.

preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.targe.description:
A list of target rule IDs under the WAF rule set to apply the preconfigured WAF exclusion.
If omitted, it refers to all the rule IDs under the WAF rule set.
preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.targe.rationale: target_rule_ids determines which specific WAF rule IDs are excluded from evaluation. If omitted, it defaults to excluding all rule IDs under the rule set, directly and significantly reducing WAF protection coverage.

preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.targe.description: Target WAF rule set to apply the preconfigured WAF exclusion.
preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.targe.rationale: target_rule_set determines which WAF rule set the exclusion applies to. Selecting the wrong or an overly broad rule set directly reduces the scope of WAF protection in effect.

preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.description: Request cookie whose value will be excluded from inspection during preconfigured WAF evaluation.

You can specify an exact match or a partial match by using a field operator and a field value.
Available options:
EQUALS: The operator matches if the field value equals the specified value.
STARTS_WITH: The operator matches if the field value starts with the specified value.
ENDS_WITH: The operator matches if the field value ends with the specified value.
CONTAINS: The operator matches if the field value contains the specified value.
EQUALS_ANY: The operator matches if the field value is any value.
preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.rationale: Defines the match breadth of a WAF exclusion applied to cookies, for example, EQUALS_ANY exempts the field entirely from inspection regardless of value. A misconfigured operator can silently widen the scope of traffic exempted from WAF protection, directly affecting exposure.

preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.description:
A request field matching the specified value will be excluded from inspection during preconfigured WAF evaluation.
The field value must be given if the field operator is not EQUALS_ANY, and cannot be given if the field operator is EQUALS_ANY.
preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.rationale: Specifies a concrete cookie value for a WAF exclusion, a generic platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain team-specific exclusion values.

preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.description: Request header whose value will be excluded from inspection during preconfigured WAF evaluation.

You can specify an exact match or a partial match by using a field operator and a field value.
Available options:
EQUALS: The operator matches if the field value equals the specified value.
STARTS_WITH: The operator matches if the field value starts with the specified value.
ENDS_WITH: The operator matches if the field value ends with the specified value.
CONTAINS: The operator matches if the field value contains the specified value.
EQUALS_ANY: The operator matches if the field value is any value.
preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.rationale: Same mechanism as request_cookie.operator: EQUALS_ANY exempts the header field entirely from WAF inspection regardless of value, directly widening exclusion scope.

preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.description:
A request field matching the specified value will be excluded from inspection during preconfigured WAF evaluation.
The field value must be given if the field operator is not EQUALS_ANY, and cannot be given if the field operator is EQUALS_ANY.
preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.rationale: Specifies a concrete header value for a WAF exclusion, this requires application-specific context that cannot be generalized into an organization-wide platform policy

preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.description:
Request query parameter whose value will be excluded from inspection during preconfigured WAF evaluation.
Note that the parameter can be in the query string or in the POST body.

You can specify an exact match or a partial match by using a field operator and a field value.
Available options:
EQUALS: The operator matches if the field value equals the specified value.
STARTS_WITH: The operator matches if the field value starts with the specified value.
ENDS_WITH: The operator matches if the field value ends with the specified value.
CONTAINS: The operator matches if the field value contains the specified value.
EQUALS_ANY: The operator matches if the field value is any value.
preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.rationale: Same mechanism as request_cookie.operator: the operator defines match breadth for excluding query parameters from WAF inspection. EQUALS_ANY exempts the field entirely from inspection regardless of value, directly widening the scope of traffic exempted from WAF protection — a misconfigured or overly broad operator here silently reduces WAF coverage over query-parameter-based attacks.

preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.description:
A request field matching the specified value will be excluded from inspection during preconfigured WAF evaluation.
The field value must be given if the field operator is not EQUALS_ANY, and cannot be given if the field operator is EQUALS_ANY.
preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.rationale: This argument references specific query parameter values to exclude from inspection, which is an application-specific configuration that a platform policy cannot generically constrain.

preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.description:
Request URI from the request line to be excluded from inspection during preconfigured WAF evaluation.
When specifying this field, the query or fragment part should be excluded.

You can specify an exact match or a partial match by using a field operator and a field value.
Available options:
EQUALS: The operator matches if the field value equals the specified value.
STARTS_WITH: The operator matches if the field value starts with the specified value.
ENDS_WITH: The operator matches if the field value ends with the specified value.
CONTAINS: The operator matches if the field value contains the specified value.
EQUALS_ANY: The operator matches if the field value is any value.
preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.rationale: Same mechanism as request_cookie.operator: the operator defines match breadth for excluding request URIs from WAF inspection. EQUALS_ANY exempts the field entirely from inspection regardless of value, directly widening the scope of traffic exempted from WAF protection — since URI paths are a common target for injection and traversal attacks, an overly broad operator here has a direct exposure impact.

preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.description:
A request field matching the specified value will be excluded from inspection during preconfigured WAF evaluation.
The field value must be given if the field operator is not EQUALS_ANY, and cannot be given if the field operator is EQUALS_ANY.
preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion.reque.rationale: Specifies a concrete URI path exempted from WAF inspection, a team-specific configuration that cannot be validated by a generic platform policy without knowing exact application routes.

redirect_options.description:
Parameters defining the redirect action. Cannot be specified for any other actions.
Note: For organization security policies, only EXTERNAL_302 redirect type is supported. GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA is not supported.

redirect_options.target.description: Target for the redirect action. This is required if the type is EXTERNAL_302.
redirect_options.target.rationale: Specifies a concrete redirect destination, a team-specific application routing choice that a generic platform policy cannot constrain without overreaching into application-level decisions.

redirect_options.type.description: Type of the redirect action. For organization security policies, only EXTERNAL_302 is supported.
redirect_options.type.rationale: Redirect_options.type is currently limited to one supported value (EXTERNAL_302) with no insecure alternative for organization security policies, so no security impact is assigned.
